lines.t: Where do I go to replace a lost student ID card?

options: No, I found mine in my backpack.
The card expires at the end of June.
The card office, on the ground floor of the student center.
Yes, it's a good idea to replace it.
optionNotes: Repeats the idea of losing/finding but answers a different question.
Repeats 'card' but gives a date, not a place.
A yes/no reply to a 'where' question.
questions.explanation: 'Where' needs a place. Only the card office answer gives one; the others reuse 'card' or 'replace'.

lines.t: Who's going to put together the slides for our presentation?

options: Maya said she'd take care of them.
Put them together on the table.
The presentation is on Friday.
I'm going to the library later.
optionNotes: Takes 'put together' literally as placing objects.
Gives a time, not a person.
Repeats 'going to' with no link to the question.
questions.explanation: 'Who' needs a person. 'Put together' here means 'prepare'.

lines.t: Would you mind if I borrowed your bike this afternoon?

options: I bought it second-hand last spring.
Yes, I'd like to borrow one too.
It takes about twenty minutes by bus.
Not at all. Just leave it by the front door when you're done.
optionNotes: Talks about the bike but never gives permission.
Repeats 'borrow' but answers as if they were the one asking.
Correct: 'Not at all' means 'I don't mind', and the speaker adds an instruction.
questions.explanation: With 'Would you mind…?', 'Not at all' gives permission. The other options never answer the request.

lines.t: Did you hear that Thursday's seminar has been moved to the main hall?

options: It moves pretty fast, doesn't it?
No, I didn't. Thanks for letting me know.
The hall lights were fixed on Thursday.
I heard a great song on the radio.
optionNotes: Correct: answers the yes/no question and thanks the speaker.
Repeats 'hall' and 'Thursday' without reacting to the news.
questions.explanation: The speaker is sharing news. A natural reply says whether you knew and reacts to it.

lines.t: Do you feel like pizza or Thai food tonight?

options: Yes, I feel much better tonight.
I had pizza for lunch, so let's do Thai.
I've never been to Thailand.
The pizza place usually gets busy around eight.
optionNotes: Correct: makes a choice and gives a reason.
Confuses Thai food with the country.
questions.explanation: A choice question (A or B) needs a choice. 'Feel like' means 'want'.

lines.t: The printer in the computer lab is out of paper again.

options: I printed my essay yesterday.
Yes, I'm out of the office again tomorrow.
It's my favorite computer lab.
There's a box of it in the cabinet by the door.
optionNotes: Repeats the idea of printing but ignores the problem.
Correct: offers a practical solution to the problem.
questions.explanation: A statement of a problem invites a solution or reaction. Only the cabinet answer helps.

lines.t: How did your meeting with your thesis advisor go?

options: Better than I expected. She liked my outline.
I'm meeting her at three.
She advises about ten students.
I'll go if you go.
optionNotes: Correct: describes how the meeting went.
Uses the future; the meeting already happened.
questions.explanation: 'How did it go?' asks for the result. 'Better than I expected' answers it.

lines.t: Is it worth getting the yearly gym membership?

options: I worked out the answer myself.
The gym is next to the swimming pool.
Only if you're going to go at least twice a week.
I've been a member of the choir for a year.
optionNotes: Correct: gives a conditional opinion about whether it is worth it.
questions.explanation: The speaker wants an opinion. The correct answer says when it is worth it.

lines.t: What time does the biology lecture start?

options: It's about cells and genetics.
Professor Grant teaches it.
I started it last year.
At nine thirty, in Room Twelve.
optionNotes: Gives the topic, not the time.
questions.explanation: 'What time' needs a time.

lines.t: Where did you go at the weekend?

options: I went by train.
I visited my aunt in Brighton.
It was really sunny.
On Saturday morning.
questions.explanation: 'Where' needs a place.

lines.t: Would you like milk in your tea?

options: I bought it at the supermarket.
I'll see you at three.
Just a little, thanks.
The milk is going up in price.
questions.explanation: An offer ('Would you like…?') needs an acceptance or a refusal.

lines.t: Is this your umbrella?

options: Yes, thanks. I must have left it here.
It's going to rain later.
No, it's my turn.
I bought a new jacket.
optionNotes: Correct: answers yes and thanks the speaker.
Related to umbrellas but does not answer.
questions.explanation: A yes/no question about ownership: 'Yes, thanks' answers it.

lines.t: How long did the math homework take you?

options: About two hours.
It's due on Friday.
I took the bus.
It was problem set three.
optionNotes: Correct: gives an amount of time.
questions.explanation: 'How long' needs a length of time.

lines.t: Do you want to watch a movie tonight?

options: I watched my little brother last night.
The cinema is downtown.
Sure. What did you have in mind?
No, I don't need a new watch.
optionNotes: Correct: accepts and asks a follow-up question.
questions.explanation: An invitation needs acceptance or refusal.

lines.t: How much did your new backpack cost?

options: I bought it at the shopping centre.
About forty pounds. It was on sale.
It's black with red straps.
I've had it for a week.
questions.explanation: 'How much' needs a price.

lines.t: The library has been packed every evening this week.

options: I packed my bag last night.
The library is open every evening.
This week I've been really busy.
It's exam season. It'll calm down after next Friday.
optionNotes: Plays on 'packed' (crowded / put things in a bag).
Repeats words but ignores the crowding.
Repeats 'this week'; about the listener, not the library.
Correct: explains why and predicts a change.
questions.explanation: 'Packed' means very crowded. The natural reply gives a reason without repeating the speaker's words.

lines.t: Could you make out what Professor Hale wrote on the board?

options: Yes, she made a great point.
She wrote a book last year.
Not a word. I'll ask her after class.
The board meets on Mondays.
optionNotes: Correct: says they could not read it and proposes a solution.
questions.explanation: 'Make out' means to read or understand with difficulty. 'Not a word' = I couldn't read anything.

lines.t: Tom hasn't done a single thing for our project.

options: Maybe we should talk to him before we go to the professor.
I think he's single, actually.
The project is due on Thursday.
Yes, he's done it twice.
optionNotes: Correct: suggests a sensible next step.
questions.explanation: A complaint invites advice or sympathy. The correct reply suggests what to do.

lines.t: I hear the new dining hall menu is pretty good.

options: Pretty good, thanks. And you?
The dining hall is next to the library.
I'll hear about it on the radio.
I wouldn't go that far. It's better than last year's, though.
optionNotes: Answers as if asked 'How are you?'.
Correct: partly disagrees in a natural way.
questions.explanation: 'I wouldn't go that far' means 'I don't completely agree'. It reacts to the opinion.

lines.t: Have you applied for on-campus housing for next year yet?

options: I applied for a job yesterday.
Not yet. I'm still on the fence about living off campus.
Next year I'll be a senior, actually.
They're building a new fence around the campus.
optionNotes: Correct: explains they have not decided.
Repeats 'next year' but never says whether they applied.
questions.explanation: 'On the fence' means undecided. That explains why they have not applied.

lines.t: I could proofread your application if you want.

options: My shoulders hurt from carrying books.
That would be a huge weight off my shoulders.
The application fee is twenty pounds.
I want to apply for the proof.
optionNotes: Mentions an unrelated physical problem; it does not respond to the offer.
Correct: accepts gratefully with an idiom.
questions.explanation: 'A weight off my shoulders' means a big relief, so it accepts the offer.

lines.t: Would you mind turning your music down a bit?

options: No, I don't mind what music you play.
I turned down the job offer last week.
It's a band from Melbourne.
Oh, sorry. I didn't realise it was that loud.
optionNotes: Talks about the music, not the volume.
Correct: apologises and implies they will do it.
questions.explanation: 'Turn down' here means make quieter. An apology is the natural response to the request.
